name: Fourth Anti-Money Laundering Directive
evidence_rating: thin: Commission assessments and an EU audit of implementation; no study measuring effects on money laundering
summary: The Commission's 2019 assessment found major divergences in how Member States apply the anti-money laundering rules, a structural weakness that led to the 2024 package replacing this Directive with a directly applicable Regulation from July 2027. The European Court of Auditors (2021) found EU action in the banking sector fragmented and implementation insufficient.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

literature.citation: European Commission (2019), Towards better implementation of the EU's anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism framework, COM(2019) 360
literature.title: Towards better implementation of the EU's anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism framework
literature.method: assessment (recent cases, supranational risk assessment, FIU cooperation)
literature.headline: Major divergences in the application of the framework; a structural problem for preventing misuse of the financial system; options include turning the Directive into a Regulation and an EU supervisor
literature.summary_plain: The Commission concluded that countries applied the anti-money laundering rules so differently that the system had structural gaps.

literature.citation: European Court of Auditors (2021), EU efforts to fight money laundering in the banking sector are fragmented and implementation is insufficient, Special Report 13/2021
literature.title: EU efforts to fight money laundering in the banking sector are fragmented and implementation is insufficient
literature.headline: Incomplete transposition of the AML directives; fragmented and poorly coordinated institutional response; EU oversight insufficient for a level playing field
literature.summary_plain: EU auditors found the rules were not fully put into national law and that supervision was fragmented.
